rubrics.criterion: The never-executable legacy quantization mode is fully removed from the extension sources: the alternative quantization implementation and its clamp-step helper no longer exist, and the live scalar quantization entry no longer contains the branch that routed to it, so no live function any longer reads the retired internal switch.
rubrics.rationale: This cluster is the heart of the instance: the dead mode appears data-dependent because the selection switch is a file-scope constant nothing ever sets, so discovering it requires connecting the live entry point to the switch's write sites, and a complete repair must edit live code rather than only delete leaf helpers.

rubrics.criterion: The unused recursive element-rendering strategy in the JSON output area is removed in full, including the mutually-calling functions and any forward declaration that exists only to close the cycle.
rubrics.rationale: The cycle's members reference each other, so each one looks called; removing the whole closed cycle rather than the first definition the solver stumbles on is the instance-specific test that reachability reasoning, not textual matching, drove the repair.

rubrics.criterion: The abandoned incremental retraining walk in the experimental IVF maintenance file is removed, together with the depth macro and policy array that exist only as its parameters.
rubrics.rationale: Distinguishing this second mutually recursive cluster from the live centroid maintenance that replaced it requires understanding which IVF paths the supported rebuild-on-invalidation design actually uses, under the experimental flag as well as without it.

rubrics.criterion: The superseded random seeding routine in the clustering helper file is removed, and the initialization routine that supported behavior actually calls is left fully intact and still in use.
rubrics.rationale: The retired seeding sits directly beside its living replacement inside one small file; a solver that cannot tell predecessor from successor will delete the wrong one or both, which the shipped tests would only partly expose.

rubrics.criterion: The draft packed chunk-blob encoding in the rescore storage area is removed entirely: the top-level draft entry and both helpers it alone connect to, along with any forward declaration introduced for them.
rubrics.rationale: Only the chain root is even a candidate for a plain unused-symbol deletion; the two helpers survive in the AST purely because the draft entry references them, so a complete repair must walk the chain its whole depth.

rubrics.criterion: The rebuild-strategy block in the DiskANN maintenance file is removed completely: the handler functions, the shared cost estimator only they call, the file-local hook table listing them, and the struct type the table was declared with.
rubrics.rationale: A file-local strategy table reads exactly like a registration point, so the handlers look dispatched; recognizing that no supported command ever walks the table is the step that distinguishes dead strategy scaffolding from live command dispatch elsewhere in the same file.

rubrics.criterion: The live scalar quantization function that hosted the never-taken branch still performs its supported transformation: its conversion of the input to the published encoded form, its memory handling, and its user-visible error behavior are unchanged from before the repair.
rubrics.rationale: The only repair site that touches a live function is the guard removal in this entry; the associated-change obligation is to leave that entry's supported semantics byte-identical while cutting the branch out of it.

rubrics.criterion: The repair removes the leftovers outright instead of resurrecting them: the patch does not set the retired internal switch to a nonzero value, add an option, command, SQL registration, or initialization path that makes any removed or previously-dead behavior reachable, and does not leave the switch present with a changed initializer just to quiet build output.
rubrics.rationale: Wiring the retired switch or table into the shipped surface would turn a dead-code cleanup into new behavior, the single likeliest wrong direction for this instance given how deliberately the leftovers mimic selectable modes.

rubrics.criterion: The scope of the deletion was decided per component under both build states of the experimental IVF compile-time flag: everything the enabled experimental build genuinely reaches stays, and every definition left dead in both build states went.
rubrics.rationale: The experimental file is only compiled when its flag is defined, so the shipped build silently hides both live experimental code and dead code there; the prompt makes auditing both states an explicit obligation and the shipped suite cannot verify it.

rubrics.criterion: No stranded companions of the removed definitions remain anywhere in the sources: no leftover forward declarations, unused spec strings, policy arrays, depth or ceiling macros, empty section remnants, or hook-table/struct leftovers whose only consumers were the deleted definitions.
rubrics.rationale: Several injected clusters intentionally carry supporting paraphernalia (a spec string, a policy table with commented meanings, a depth macro, a strategy struct) so that deleting only the flagged functions would leave obviously-orphaned artifacts behind; the cleanup obligation is instance-specific, not generic style.

rubrics.criterion: The patch does not leave any dangling reference to what it removed: no remaining declaration, table entry, comment-documented call contract, macro use, or string literal naming a deleted definition survives in the translation unit.
rubrics.rationale: Because the extension is one translation unit, half-removals here surface as compile errors only some of the time; stale references that still parse (a leftover forward declaration, a fresh spec string) are the concrete residue this instance invites.

rubrics.criterion: The patch does not delete experimental-flag-gated definitions that the enabled build legitimately uses (the live centroid maintenance, clustering and query paths of the experimental component), whose absence the shipped build's test run would not reveal.
rubrics.rationale: The shipped suite skips the experimental component when its flag is off, so over-deletion inside it is precisely the regression this task's determinant suite cannot catch; it is the most credible silent breakage available to a sloppy repair.

rubrics.criterion: The patch does not remove any definition still executed under the shipped configuration: the current quantizer, the single-pass JSON builder, the initializer used in supported clustering, the chunk-blob storage path used by inserts and updates, and the incremental reverse-edge repair all remain and still run where they did before.
rubrics.rationale: Every dead cluster sits next to a surviving lookalike with a similar name and shape; mislocalization would delete a live neighbor, and parts of that loss (storage formats, graph repair) surface only in specific vec0 configurations rather than the suite's most common paths.

rubrics.criterion: Removing the never-taken branch from the live quantization entry did not disturb its surrounding control flow: the cleaned function's supported results, output subtype and memory ownership are identical, with no restructured cleanup path, dropped error handling, or altered early-return behavior introduced alongside the deletion.
rubrics.rationale: The guard-branch removal is the one edit to a live function's body, and the natural implementation slip is to 'simplify' the entry's cleanup or error path while inside it; the instance-specific risk is collateral control-flow change at this single live site.
